control-absorb-pointer.summary: Blocks taps and other pointer input to its `content` while `absorbing` is true, and keeps them from reaching the controls behind it as well. Use it to lock a form while it saves: unlike `disabled`, the content keeps its normal look. To let taps pass through to whatever lies behind instead, use [`ignore_pointer`](/docs/control-ignore-pointer). The other pointer wrappers and sizing boxes are in [Controls and Layout](/docs/controls-and-layout#transitions-clips-and-sizing-boxes).

control-clip-oval.summary: Clips its `content` to the oval that fills the content's box: a circle for a square box, an ellipse otherwise. Use it for round avatars and thumbnails. For rounded corners, see [`clip_rsuperellipse`](/docs/control-clip-r-superellipse) and the other clips in [Controls and Layout](/docs/controls-and-layout#transitions-clips-and-sizing-boxes).

control-clip-r-superellipse.summary: Clips its `content` to a rectangle whose corners follow a continuous curve (a superellipse, the iOS "squircle"), which looks smoother than the circular corners of a container's `border_radius`. `border_radius` takes one radius for every corner or one per corner. Build it with `clip_rsuperellipse`; the other clips are in [Controls and Layout](/docs/controls-and-layout#transitions-clips-and-sizing-boxes).

control-cupertino-date-picker.summary: An iOS-style wheel for picking a date, a time, or both. Open it with `page.show_dialog(picker)`: on iOS and macOS the wheel slides up with Cancel and Done, and on Android, web, Windows and Linux the client shows the Material date picker dialog. When the user confirms, `on_change` gets the picked moment in `event.data`, an ISO 8601 string in UTC. With 0.0.23 a picker added to the page shows nothing; drawing it in place with `page.add` (the wheel on iOS and macOS, a calendar elsewhere) needs the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-drag-target.summary: A drop zone for [`draggable`](/docs/control-draggable) controls. It accepts a draggable whose `group` matches its own, and its events tell you when one enters, moves over, leaves or is dropped. `event.src_id` is the dropped draggable's id: `page.get_control(event.src_id)` returns that control. The client moves nothing itself, so change the page in `on_accept`.
example: status = text(value: "Drag the photo into the album")
box = container(width: 200, height: 140, bgcolor: "#f1f5f9", border_radius: 12, alignment: "center", content: text("Album"))

control-draggable.summary: Lets the user pick up its `content` and drop it on a [`drag_target`](/docs/control-drag-target) of the same `group`. While it is dragged, `content_feedback` (by default the content at half opacity) follows the pointer and `content_when_dragging` stays in its place. Nothing moves on its own: the target's `on_accept` decides what a drop does, and the draggable's `on_drag_complete` fires when a target accepted it.
example: status = text(value: "Drag a task onto Done")
container(width: 140, padding: 12, bgcolor: "#dbeafe", border_radius: 8, content: text(title)),
container(width: 160, height: 120, bgcolor: "#dcfce7", border_radius: 12, padding: 12, content: text("Done")),

control-fractionally-sized-box.summary: Sizes its `content` to a fraction of the space its parent offers: `width_factor: 0.5` makes it half as wide. The parent must bound that axis, so place it in a sized `container`, an expanded control or a `stack`, not directly in a `row`, `column` or scrolling list along their scroll direction, where the client shows an error. More sizing boxes are in [Controls and Layout](/docs/controls-and-layout#transitions-clips-and-sizing-boxes).

control-hero.summary: Flies a control from one view to the next: when the app pushes or pops a view, the `hero` on the old view moves and resizes into the place of the `hero` with the same `tag` on the new view, as a thumbnail that grows into its detail page. Both views need a hero with that tag. Build the view stack with `page.views`, as in [Navigation and Feedback](/docs/navigation-feedback).
example: content: hero(image(photo, width: 160, height: 100, fit: "cover"), tag: "lake"),

control-ignore-pointer.summary: Makes its `content` ignore taps and other pointer input while `ignoring` is true; the input goes to whatever lies behind it, such as a control lower in a `stack`. Use it for labels and decorations drawn over a clickable surface. To block the input altogether, use [`absorb_pointer`](/docs/control-absorb-pointer).
example: on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "The card got the tap") }
content: text("This label lets taps through", style: { size: 16 })

control-interactive-viewer.summary: Lets the user pan and zoom its `content` with drags, pinches and the mouse wheel, for images, maps and diagrams. The zoom stays between `min_scale` and `max_scale`, and Ruby can change it with `zoom`, `pan`, `reset`, `save_state` and `restore_state` once the viewer is on the page. The interaction events carry raw data: read it from `event.data`.
example: zoom = text(value: "Pinch or scroll to zoom")

control-intrinsic-height.summary: Sizes its `content` to the content's own natural height. Wrap a `row` in it so that `vertical_alignment: "stretch"` gives every child the height of the tallest one. It costs an extra layout pass, so use it for small rows, not long lists. More sizing boxes are in [Controls and Layout](/docs/controls-and-layout#transitions-clips-and-sizing-boxes).
example: card = ->(label) { container(padding: 12, bgcolor: "#e0e7ff", border_radius: 8, content: text(label)) }

control-intrinsic-width.summary: Sizes its `content` to the content's own natural width, so a `column` of buttons with `horizontal_alignment: "stretch"` makes every button as wide as the widest one. `step_width` and `step_height` round the size up to a multiple. Like [`intrinsic_height`](/docs/control-intrinsic-height), it costs an extra layout pass.

control-keyboard-listener.summary: Sends `on_key_down`, `on_key_up` and `on_key_repeat` for keys pressed while it has keyboard focus. Give it `autofocus: true`, or let the user focus a control inside it, or it receives no keys. `event.data[:key]` is the key's label, such as `"A"`, `"Enter"` or `"Arrow Down"`.

control-merge-semantics.summary: Makes screen readers announce its `content` as one element, so a rating row made of an icon and two texts is read as one item instead of three separate stops. It changes nothing on screen. To describe a control in your own words, use [`semantics`](/docs/control-semantics).

control-overlay.summary: The page's overlay layer: controls in it are drawn above the current view, for toasts, floating panels and loading veils. Add a control with `page.overlay << control` (or assign `page.overlay = [...]`) and call `page.update`; delete it from `page.overlay` to remove it. An overlay control sits at the top left unless you place it with `align`, as the example does; `left`, `top`, `right` and `bottom` work only inside a `stack`. The `overlay(...)` helper builds the layer itself, which only the page uses: the client cannot draw it as an ordinary child.

control-placeholder.summary: Draws a box with a cross through it where a control will go, for sketching a layout before the real content exists. It fills the size its parent gives it, or `fallback_width` by `fallback_height` (400 each) where the parent leaves a size open, as in a `row`.
example: placeholder(text("Chart goes here"), width: 200, height: 80, color: "#2563eb", stroke_width: 1)

control-popup-menu-item.summary: One entry in a [`popup_menu_button`](/docs/control-popup-menu-button) menu, with text, an icon, or both. Set `checked` for a check mark. The client does not change it, so keep the state yourself and update `checked` in `on_click`: `event.data` is `true` or `nil`, never `false`, and the 0.0.23 client on iOS and macOS sends none. Leave out both text and icon for a divider. Icons, check marks and dividers show on Android, web, Windows and Linux only: on iOS and macOS the menu shows each item's text and nothing else, and an item without text draws an error box.
example: popup_menu_item("Name", icon: "sort_by_alpha", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by name") }),
popup_menu_item("Date", icon: "event", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by date") }),

control-reorderable-drag-handle.summary: Marks the part of a [`reorderable_list_view`](/docs/control-reorderable-list-view) item that the user drags to move it, such as a grip icon. Set `show_default_drag_handles: false` on the list so that only your handles start a drag. Outside a reorderable list it shows an error.

control-rotated-box.summary: Turns its `content` by whole quarter turns and lays it out turned: a box turned by one quarter takes its height as its width, so the controls around it make room. Use it for vertical labels. For other angles, use the `rotate` property, which turns the drawing but keeps the unrotated layout.
example: container(width: 200, height: 120, bgcolor: "#f1f5f9", padding: 12, content: text("The rotated label takes its rotated size, so the row leaves room for it."))

control-rotation-transition.summary: Spins its `content` from `begin` to `end`, counted in full turns, on the client. With `repeat: true` it is a loading spinner that costs Ruby nothing per frame, and `page.update(spinner, animating: false)` pauses it. It takes the timing keywords of [`fade_transition`](/docs/control-fade-transition).
example: spinner = rotation_transition(icon("sync", size: 40), duration: 1200, curve: "linear", repeat: true)
text_button(content: text("Pause"), on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(spinner, animating: false) }),
text_button(content: text("Resume"), on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(spinner, animating: true) })

control-ruflet-app.summary: Embeds another Ruflet app, served at `url`, inside this page, for example a live preview of a second app or a dashboard widget. The embedded app runs its own session on its own server, and the errors it reports arrive in `on_error`.
example: text("Live preview of the dashboard app"),

control-scale-transition.summary: Scales its `content` from `begin` to `end` around `alignment`, on the client, for pop-in effects and pulsing badges. It takes the timing keywords of [`fade_transition`](/docs/control-fade-transition); `on_animation_end` gets `"transition"` when a run that does not repeat finishes.

control-screenshot.summary: Captures its `content` as a PNG image. Call `capture` on the mounted control; `on_result` gets the PNG bytes as a binary String, or an error. Pass `pixel_ratio:` as a Float such as `2.0`, which works with every release. An Integer `pixel_ratio:` needs the next release: the 0.0.23 client returns an error for it. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
example: content: column(children: [text("Order #1042", style: { size: 18, weight: "bold" }), text("2 items, $24.00")])
page.update(status, value: error ? error.to_s : "Captured #{png.to_s.bytesize} bytes of PNG")

control-segment.summary: One option of a [`segmented_button`](/docs/control-segmented-button). `value` is required, and is what the button reports in `selected` and `on_change`; `label` and `icon` are what the user sees.
example: segment("grid", label: "Grid", icon: icon("grid_view"), tooltip: "Show a grid"),
segment("map", label: "Map", icon: icon("map"), disabled: true)

control-selection-area.summary: Lets the user select text across every `text` control inside its `content` at once and copy it, instead of one selectable text at a time. `on_change` reports the selected text.
example: text("Build Flutter apps in Ruby. Select across both lines to copy them together.")

control-semantics.summary: Describes its `content` to screen readers such as VoiceOver and TalkBack: a `label`, a `value`, a role such as `button` or `slider`, and the actions they can trigger, such as `on_increase`. It changes nothing on screen. Drawing the wrapped `content` needs the next release: the 0.0.23 client draws nothing for a `semantics` control, so the wrapped control disappears, and until then the controls' own `semantics_label` is the way to label them. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).
control-semantics.example_callout: With 0.0.23 the client draws nothing for a `semantics` control, so the container in this example disappears.
example: container(width: 200, height: 24, bgcolor: "#dbeafe", border_radius: 12, content: level),

control-shader-mask.summary: Paints a gradient through its `content`. With `blend_mode: "srcIn"` the gradient shows only where the content is, as in gradient text; other blend modes fade or tint the content. `shader` is required: a gradient hash whose `_type` is `"linear"`, `"radial"` or `"sweep"`.

control-shimmer.summary: Sweeps a moving highlight across its `content`: the loading skeleton effect. Lay out grey boxes in the shape of the coming content, wrap them in `shimmer`, and replace the shimmer when the data arrives. It needs `base_color` and `highlight_color`, or a `gradient`.
example: line = ->(width) { container(width: width, height: 14, bgcolor: "#d1d5db", border_radius: 4) }

control-size-transition.summary: Grows or shrinks its `content` along `axis` between `begin` and `end`, fractions of the content's size, and clips the part that does not fit yet, for sections that open and close. A new `end` sent with `page.update` animates from the size shown now, as in the example. It takes the timing keywords of [`fade_transition`](/docs/control-fade-transition).
example: container(padding: 12, bgcolor: "#f1f5f9", content: text("Delivery in 2-3 days. Free returns within 30 days.")),

control-slide-transition.summary: Slides its `content` from `begin` to `end`, offsets counted in fractions of the content's own size, so `{ x: -1, y: 0 }` starts one width to the left. Use `delay` to stagger a list of items, as in the example. It takes the timing keywords of [`fade_transition`](/docs/control-fade-transition).

control-sliver-fill-remaining.summary: Fills the space the other slivers of a [`custom_scroll_view`](/docs/control-custom-scroll-view) leave in the viewport, for an empty state or a footer at the bottom of a short list. When the slivers above already fill the screen, it is only as tall as its content. Like every sliver, it takes only its own keywords plus `key`, `data` and `visible`; layout keywords such as `expand` raise ArgumentError.

control-sliver-grid.summary: A grid among the slivers of a [`custom_scroll_view`](/docs/control-custom-scroll-view), scrolling together with them. Set the number of columns with `runs_count`, or the largest cell width with `max_extent` so the grid fits as many columns as the width allows. Like every sliver, it takes only its own keywords plus `key`, `data` and `visible`; layout keywords such as `expand` raise ArgumentError.
example: sliver_to_box_adapter(container(padding: 16, content: text("Photos", style: { size: 22, weight: "bold" }))),

control-sliver-list.summary: A list among the slivers of a [`custom_scroll_view`](/docs/control-custom-scroll-view), scrolling together with them; items are built as they scroll into view. A `header` with `sticky_header: true` stays at the top while its items pass under it and leaves with the list, as the section letters of a contacts list do. Like every sliver, it takes only its own keywords plus `key`, `data` and `visible`; layout keywords such as `expand` raise ArgumentError.
example: header: container(padding: 8, bgcolor: "#e5e7eb", content: text(letter, weight: "bold")),

control-sliver-padding.summary: Insets one or more slivers of a [`custom_scroll_view`](/docs/control-custom-scroll-view) by `padding`; they scroll as one group. A plain control among them scrolls as a box. Like every sliver, it takes only its own keywords plus `key`, `data` and `visible`; layout keywords such as `expand` raise ArgumentError.

control-sliver-to-box-adapter.summary: Places one ordinary control, such as a heading or a profile card, among the slivers of a [`custom_scroll_view`](/docs/control-custom-scroll-view). A plain control listed directly in `slivers` is wrapped the same way, so the helper mostly makes the intent explicit. Like every sliver, it takes only its own keywords plus `key`, `data` and `visible`; layout keywords such as `expand` raise ArgumentError.
example: content: row(spacing: 12, children: [circle_avatar(text("AL")), text("Ada Lovelace", style: { size: 18 })])

control-text-span.summary: A piece of inline text in a `text` control's `spans`, with its own `style`, a link (`url`) or a tap handler (`on_click`). Spans nest through their own `spans`. A span is not drawn on its own: put it in `text(..., spans: [...])`.

control-transparent-pointer.summary: Lets its `content` receive taps and other pointer input and also passes that input on to the controls behind it, so two controls layered in a `stack` both react to one tap. Without it, a `stack` gives each tap only to the topmost control under the pointer.
example: on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "The square got the tap") }
page.update(status, value: "Tap at #{point.x.round}, #{point.y.round} reached the square too") if point

control-vertical-divider.summary: A thin vertical line between controls in a `row`, the counterpart of [`divider`](/docs/control-divider). `width` is the space it takes and `thickness` the line itself. It is as tall as the row lets it be, so give the row a height, as the example does: a row in a column has no height of its own.

control-window-drag-area.summary: Turns its `content` into a handle that moves the desktop window, for a custom title bar on Windows, macOS and Linux. Double-clicking it maximizes or restores the window, unless `maximizable: false`.
example: status = text(value: "Drag the dark bar to move the window; double-click it to maximize")
